mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +9.4% (t-0w) after a four-week climb from +8.6%. This sustained elevation signals household confinement is plateauing, releasing pent-up demand for retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from +8.6% to +9.7% then stabilized at +9.4%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +8.5% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations have contracted to -39.1% (t-0w) from a low of -42.3% (t-1w), signaling a marginal recovery in commuting. This rebound in transit use will drive retail-and-recreation mobility upward as workers resume in-person activity patterns.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -42.3% to -39.1% over one week
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not sustain improvement beyond -39.1% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines in weeks 1-2 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated monotonically from -3.6% (t-3w) to -9.6% (t-1w), then partially recovered to -7.9% (t-0w). This reversal in outdoor recreation signals renewed appetite for discretionary mobility, which will extend to retail-and-recreation venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 1 percentage point from t-0w baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -9.6% to -7.9% in one week
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve further in week 1 of the forecast, or RETAIL_REC declines in week 1 despite PARKS improvement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are jointly suppressed, with GROCERY_PHARM at -16.6% (t-0w). A recovery in essential-goods mobility (GROCERY_PHARM rising above -15%) will unlock retail-and-recreation visits as consumers resume integrated shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15% in any week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not rise above -15% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite GROCERY_PHARM recovery.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -46.3% (t-0w) after declining to -51.6% (t-1w). If workplace restrictions ease and WORKPLACES rises above -45% within one week, retail-and-recreation will follow as commuting infrastructure reactivates.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not exceed -45% in week 1, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES improvement.

mechanism_narrative: All mobility categories show stabilization or marginal recovery at t-0w after deterioration at t-1w. This inflection point signals the end of a contraction phase. Retail-and-recreation will rebound over the next four weeks as the baseline regime shifts from tightening to stabilization.
evidence_refs: fact:All three series improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or any of the three proxies deteriorates below t-0w levels in weeks 1-2.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has oscillated narrowly between -44.9% and -41.1% over four weeks with no trend. This persistent suppression will continue unchanged over the next four weeks absent a shock to WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, as retail demand remains structurally constrained.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC range is -44.9% to -41.1% with no directional trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -40% in any week of the forecast period, or WORKPLACES exceeds -40% triggering demand recovery.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (+9.4%) combined with WORKPLACES suppression (-46.3%) indicates home-based activity dominance. If WORKPLACES remains below -45% and RESIDENTIAL stays above +9%, retail-and-recreation will remain depressed as the population remains confined to residential spaces.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -45% AND RESIDENTIAL remains above +9%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -40% in any week, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +8%, or RETAIL_REC increases above -40% despite both conditions holding.
